claims.claim: **Most children with petechiae do not have serious bacterial infection or meningococcal disease**, and often no cause is found. ⚠️ **Seriously unwell children with petechiae/purpura need urgent management.**
claims.source_text: The majority of children with petechiae do not have a serious bacterial infection or meningococcal disease, and often will not have a specific cause identified Seriously unwell children with petechiae/purpura require urgent management
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Serious bacterial infection, including meningococcal disease, can present with a non-blanching rash with or without fever.** Pneumococcal and meningococcal bacteraemia have fallen since routine vaccination.
claims.source_text: Serious bacterial infections including meningococcal disease can present with a non-blanching rash, with or without fever … The incidence of pneumococcal and meningococcal bacteraemia has decreased since the introduction of routine vaccination
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Petechiae and purpura do not blanch.** Glass test: press a drinking glass firmly on the rash — if it does not disappear, it is non-blanching. **Petechiae are pinpoint; purpura are larger (over 2 mm).**
claims.source_text: Both petechiae and purpura do not blanch when pressure is applied … The 'glass test' can be used to assist with assessing whether a rash is blanching - a drinking glass can be applied firmly against a rash - if the rash does not disappear it is non-blanching … Petechiae are pinpoint non-blanching spots Purpura are larger non-blanching spots (>2 mm)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **All children with fever and petechiae/purpura should be reviewed promptly by a senior clinician.**
claims.source_text: All children with fever and petechiae/purpura should be reviewed promptly by a senior clinician
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Higher-risk history:** under 6 months or incompletely immunised · rapid onset or progression · **prior antibiotics may mask bacterial infection** · immunosuppression or previous invasive bacterial infection.
claims.source_text: Immunisation status - children <6 months of age or with incomplete immunisation status Rapid onset and/or rapid progression of symptoms and rash Medications: prior treatment with antibiotics may mask signs of a bacterial infection High risk groups: immunosuppression, previous invasive bacterial infections
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **The child is unwell if:** abnormal vital signs (tachycardia, tachypnoea, desaturation in air) · **cold shock** (narrow pulse pressure, cold extremities, prolonged refill) · **warm shock** (wide pulse pressure, bounding pulses, flushed skin, rapid refill) · altered conscious state (inconsolable crying, lethargy) · limb tenderness or difficulty mobilising.
claims.source_text: Children are considered unwell when they have: Abnormal vital signs: tachycardia, tachypnoea and/or desaturation in air Cold shock: narrow pulse pressure, cold extremities, prolonged capillary refill Warm shock: wide pulse pressure, bounding pulses, flushed skin with rapid capillary refill Altered conscious state: irritability (inconsolable crying or screaming), lethargy (including as reported by family or other staff) Limb tenderness or difficulty mobilising
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In every child, look for haematological causes:** hepatomegaly or splenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, joint swelling or erythema.
claims.source_text: For all children, also consider haematological causes and review for: Hepatomegaly or splenomegaly Lymphadenopathy Swelling or erythema of joints
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mechanical:** vomiting or coughing (petechiae in the superior vena cava distribution, above the nipples) · local pressure (holding, tight tourniquet) · non-accidental or accidental injury.
claims.source_text: Mechanical Vomiting or coughing - occurs in the distribution of the superior vena cava which is above the level of the nipples Local physical pressure eg holding child during procedure, tight tourniquet Non-accidental injury or accidental injury
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Infective:** enterovirus, adenovirus, influenza; *N. meningitidis*, *S. pneumoniae*, *H. influenzae*, group A streptococcus, *S. aureus*.
claims.source_text: Viral Enterovirus Adenovirus Influenza Bacterial Neisseria meningitidis (meningococcal disease) Streptococcus pneumoniae Haemophilus influenzae Group A streptococcus Staphylococcus aureus
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Haematological and other:** ITP · malignancy including acute leukaemia · aplastic anaemia · DIC · HUS · Henoch-Schönlein purpura · vasculitis · drug-induced thrombocytopenia.
claims.source_text: Haematological Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) Malignancy including acute leukaemia Aplastic anaemia Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) Haemolytic uraemic syndrome (HUS) Other Henoch-Schönlein purpura (HSP) Vasculitis Drug-induced thrombocytopenia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Any newborn with petechiae needs prompt senior review** — consider congenital CMV, toxoplasmosis and neonatal lupus as well.
claims.source_text: There are additional causes of petechiae that should be considered in newborns (eg congenital cytomegalovirus, toxoplasmosis, neonatal lupus). Any newborn with petechiae should be promptly reviewed with a senior clinician
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If no senior clinician is available, manage by the flowchart** — the safest approach. A blood film must be reviewed to exclude an alternative diagnosis.
claims.source_text: If a senior clinician is unavailable, the safest approach is to manage according to the flowchart. … Film must be reviewed to exclude an alternative diagnosis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ceftriaxone 100 mg/kg (max 4 g) IV daily.** ⚠️ Avoid where possible in neonates under 41 weeks' gestation, especially if jaundiced or receiving calcium-containing solutions including TPN.
claims.source_text: Ceftriaxone: 100 mg/kg (4 g) IV daily (where possible, ceftriaxone should be avoided in neonates <41 weeks gestation, particularly if jaundiced or receiving calcium containing solutions, including TPN)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cefotaxime 50 mg/kg (max 2 g) IV** — 12-hourly in week 1 of life, 6–8-hourly in weeks 2–4, 6-hourly after week 4.
claims.source_text: Cefotaxime: 50 mg/kg (2 g) IV 12H (week 1 of life), 6-8H (week 2-4 of life), 6H (>week 4 of life)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the paediatric team** for any unwell child including suspected meningococcal disease, diagnostic uncertainty or follow-up, and escalation advice.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when Assessing any unwell child, including any with suspected meningococcal disease Uncertainty about diagnosis or to arrange follow-up Advice regarding escalation of care
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Petechiae and purpura' (Last updated February 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_and_Petechiae_Purpura/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when a serious cause is unlikely** on assessment and/or investigations — and **always advise return if the child becomes more unwell.**
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when Serious cause of petechiae/purpura considered unlikely based on clinical assessment and/or investigations Always advise parents to return for review if their child becomes more unwell or there is concern
